The first kings of [[Galar]] are characters from the backstory of [[Pokémon Sword and Shield]].

{{spoilers}}

==In the core series games==
===History===
====Background====
3,000 years prior to the events of the games, in an event called the [[Darkest Day]], a powerful [[Legendary Pokémon]] named {{p|Eternatus}} awakened from its 17,000 year slumber and created a huge storm in the skies of the [[Galar]] region, causing many Pokémon all over the region to [[Dynamax|grow gigantic]] and go berserk, destroying everything in their path. The two youths eventually encountered and joined forces with {{p|Zacian}} and {{p|Zamazenta}}, who had also awakened to protect the region from Eternatus's rage. Using their [[Rusted Sword|sword]] and [[Rusted Shield|shield]], the youths, Zacian, and Zamazenta defeated Eternatus, forcing it to return to its slumber for 3000 more years. After the battle concluded, the two youths were crowned as kings of Galar. Statues of the two kings and the two Pokémon were also built at some point in [[Stow-on-Side]], depicting the kings as tall men wearing royal clothes.

===={{g|Sword and Shield}}====
By the present day, the true story of the Darkest Day had been forgotten, and various alternate versions of the story arose: one about a single young hero defeating all gigantic Pokémon with their sword and shield (honored by a golden statue in the hall of the {{DL|Motostoke|Budew Drop Inn}}, which depicts them as a tall armored man wielding a sword and a shield), and another about two youths managing to stop the Darkest Day with the use of a sword and a shield, being crowned as kings as a result (retold in the four tapestries in the [[Hammerlocke]] vault, which depict them as a dark-haired youth wearing blue and a blonde youth wearing red). All of these retellings typically obscure the identities of Zacian and Zamazenta and undersell their roles during the Darkest Day in favor of the kings, causing the two Pokémon to also be forgotten throughout modern-day Galar.

During the events of {{g|Sword and Shield}}, [[Sonia]] looks into the conflicting accounts and finds out what had truly happened due to discovering the statues of the two kings and the two Pokémon, which had been hidden behind a colorful ancient mural. She publishes her findings in her book: [[Sonia's Book|Galar: A History]]. Later on, when [[Rose]] awakens {{p|Eternatus}} and brings about the second [[Darkest Day]], [[Hop]] and [[Victor]]/[[Gloria]] become their successors as they use the [[Rusted Sword]] and [[Rusted Shield]] to call {{p|Zacian}} and {{p|Zamazenta}} and take down Eternatus. In the post-game, the brothers [[Sordward]] and [[Shielbert]] claim to be the kings' descendants and contest Sonia's book, but they eventually drop their claim to the throne when they apologize for their actions.

==In animation==
[[File:Stow-on-Side statues anime.png|thumb|250px|Statues of the kings in {{aniseries|JN}}]]
===''[[Pokémon the Series]]''===
===={{aniseries|JN}}====
Instead of being in the [[Motostoke#Budew Drop Inn|Budew Drop Inn]] like in the games, the statue of the single, legendary hero is in [[Wyndon Stadium]]. In ''[[JN027|Toughing It Out!]]'', {{Ash}} and [[Goh]] notice the statue and wonder if it depicts {{an|Leon}}. However, [[Sonia]] explains that it depicts a legendary hero who saved [[Galar]] from a [[Darkest Day|terrible storm]] and rampaging [[Dynamax|giant]] Pokémon.

In ''[[JN043|Sword and Shield: The Darkest Day!]]'', Sonia shows Goh a picture of the [[Hammerlocke]] Vault's tapestries, which she believes depict the origins of the Galar region. Goh says that the tapestries depict the two heroes who worked together to fight off the Darkest Day. Sonia concludes that this means the legend of the one single hero is wrong.

In ''[[JN043|Sword and Shield: The Darkest Day!]]'', while [[Goh]] battles [[Oleana's subordinate]], his {{TP|Goh|Raboot}} accidentally destroys the mural in [[Stow-on-Side]], revealing the statues of the kings alongside the {{an|legendary heroes}}. In the [[JN044|next episode]], Goh and Sonia spot the statues and the former recognizes {{an|legendary heroes#Zacian|Zacian}} and {{an|legendary heroes#Zamazenta|Zamazenta}} from when he explored the [[Slumbering Weald]] alongside Ash.

==In the manga==
[[File:Stow-on-Side statues Adventures.png|thumb|200px|Sculptures of the kings in [[Pokémon Adventures]]]]
===[[Pokémon Adventures]]===
In ''[[PASS05|Ooh Shiny!! Legendary Equipment]]'', {{adv|Henry}} and {{adv|Casey}} travel to [[Motostoke]] and spot the statue of the single, legendary hero in [[Motostoke#Budew Drop Inn|Budew Drop Inn]] at [[Motostoke]]. In the [[PASS06|next chapter]], Casey notices the sword and shield and Henry notes that they kind of resemble the [[Rusted Sword]] and [[Rusted Shield|Shield]]. [[Sonia]] also explains that according to legend, the hero once saved region from a [[Darkest Day|black vortex]] that transformed many Pokémon into [[Dynamax|giants]].

In ''[[PASS12|Thump!! The Gazing Sage]]'', Henry, Sonia, and [[Raihan]] enter the [[Hammerlocke]] Vault and see its tapestries. In the [[PASS13|next chapter]], the trio analyze the different tapestures and uncover the history behind the Darkest Day which starts out of nowhere, but is stopped by the two youths. Henry also notes that sword and shield wielded by the youths are similar to the Rusted Sword and Shield and the ones wielded by the hero statue at Budew Drop Inn.

In ''[[PASS20|Cracking!! Brilliant Tap-Dancing]]'', Sonia shows Henry, Casey, and [[Marvin]] a picture of statue of the kings alongside the [[Legendary heroes#Pokémon Adventures|legendary heroes]] after [[Bede]] destroyed the mural on [[Stow-on-Side]] in ''[[PASS14|Teary!! The Voice of the Master]]''. The latter two recognize the sword and shield Pokémon and Sonia theorizes that someone tried to give all the credit to the humans. Additionally, the group travels to [[Circhester#Bob's Your Uncle|Bob's Your Uncle]] in [[Circhester]] where Sonia shows them a fourth tapestry from the Hammerlocke Vault, which depicts the two youths being crowned kings. Sonia claims it was thrown away to be erased from history.
